I'm putting together the structured output from this Chinese delivery note, number SN-260730-216 from Dongguan Precision Housings, dated 2026-07-30. It covers two purchase orders and two part lines, with the quantities and package counts for each.

I'm reading the stamp, signature and remarks fields, and noting that the file's date doesn't appear on the document itself. The quantities use a period as the decimal mark, so 134.000 and 23.000 read as 134 and 23 pieces, while the package totals still add up to 279.

I'm settling on reading the quantities as 134 and 23 pieces, since the period works as a decimal mark here, and I'll flag that reading as ambiguous. The 3069 kg gross weight works out to about 11 kg per package, which fits steel cases, so I'll record it as a shipment-level statement rather than on a line. The stamp overlaps the PCS and package-count cells, but the numbers are still legible, so I'll mark them clear and note the overlap.

I'm filling in the issuer and recipient, Dongguan Precision Housings and Soony Distribution Center in Hamburg, along with the two PO numbers and the delivery note reference. I'm noting there are no decisions or corrections, that the receipt signature is blank, and that the stamp partly covers the table but the document still reads as clean. The open question is which purchase order each line belongs to, since the document doesn't say.
